subject: Mapping revenue splits and invoice/ledger flows for SkyForge integration
messages:
From: Ravi Shah <ravi@skyforge.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@quantops.co>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mapping revenue splits for integration partnership

Hey Camila,

Thanks again for the call earlier — excited to move the SkyForge <> Redwood integration into a commercial test. Before we open the first co-sell opportunities, can you share a recommended revenue-split and the accounting / invoicing flow so our finance team can map it to our ledger? Specifically we need: 

- The split by product line (hosted API vs dedicated capacity) and where referral vs reseller credits apply
- Invoicing cadence and whether Redwood will send consolidated monthly invoices to us or we invoice partners directly for our share
- Any lead-registration guardrails (stale-window, proof of introduction) so we can agree to credits up front

We have an internal deadline to finish mapping by 4/30 so would appreciate a short doc or spreadsheet. Attaching our MOU excerpt as reference (see inline).

Best,
Ravi
Head of Strategic Partnerships
SkyForge Analytics
(attachment: SkyForge_MOU_excerpt.pdf)

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ravi Shah <ravi@skyforge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mapping revenue splits for integration partnership

Ravi —

Appreciate the clear asks. I've drafted a starting commission schedule and a proposed invoicing flow (see attached). High level summary below: 

- Proposed splits: 70/30 host-API revenue split in favor of Redwood for self-serve hosted API; 50/50 for Dedicated capacity where customer signs a reserved-contract through SkyForge as the reseller. Referral credits: 10% finder fee on first 12 months of ARR for pure referrals that do not result in resale.
- Ledger mapping: Redwood issues consolidated monthly settlement statements. For reseller bookings where SkyForge invoices the end-customer directly, Redwood will net-settle monthly and provide a CSV mapping (GL codes included) for your AP to post against.
- Invoicing cadence: Monthly settlements with 30-day payment terms from Redwood to partner. Partner invoices for their reseller margin to Redwood (or Redwood to partner depending on lead pathway) — detailed flow is in the spreadsheet.
- Lead registration: 90-day exclusivity window after registration; credit requires HubSpot ticket id + first-touch email thread. Stale-window: registrations not converted within 12 months expire.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben can review the deal-level exceptions (discounts, credits) and confirm whether the split applies to trial credits/overage tokens.
2) Marissa will align the partner ops playbook and update the lead registration form with the proof checklist.
3) Ravi/Elena confirm that monthly CSV settlement fields align to SkyForge GL mapping.

Attaching: Commission_Schedule_V1.xlsx (spreadsheet) — contains line items and a sample monthly settlement CSV.

If this looks OK, we can lock a doc for legal to convert into a short addendum.

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0124
(attachment: Commission_Schedule_V1.xlsx)

From: Ravi Shah <ravi@skyforge.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@quantops.co>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 12:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mapping revenue splits for integration partnership

Camila —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and useful spreadsheet. A couple of clarification requests from our finance/ops side: 

- For the 50/50 Dedicated split, does Redwood gross-book the full contract and remit SkyForge's share, or will SkyForge invoice and Redwood remit net? Our AP prefers to gross-book only when we hold the contract. If Redwood will gross-book, we need the monthly CSV to include contract id, booking date, and tax breakdown.
- Lead registration: the 90-day exclusivity is fine, but can we add a step that any registration over $100k ARR requires a joint outreach within 30 days or the registration becomes non-exclusive? That's important for our channel managers.
- Invoicing: 30-day payment term is workable, but can Redwood support ACH transfers and include an invoice reference field for our ERP (we use NetSuite)?

Couple of small asks — if you and Ben can confirm the gross-booking behavior and include the tax/contract id fields in the CSV, we can sign off and take to our legal for a short addendum.

Appreciate it —
Ravi
Ravi Shah
Head of Strategic Partnerships, SkyForge Analytics

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mapping revenue splits for integration partnership

Ravi / Camila —

Quick note from deal ops and finance: Redwood prefers to gross-book reseller contracts when the partner is the named seller on the master service agreement. For cases where SkyForge invoices directly to your customer, Redwood will perform net settlements monthly. I've attached our sample invoice template and the required CSV fields for NetSuite mapping. Highlights: 

- We will include contract id, booking date, tax breakdown, and invoice_reference in the CSV.
- ACH support: yes — we'll include banking instructions on the settlement PDF and our AP contact.
- For the registration > $100k ARR ask, Camila and I are fine with the 30-day joint outreach requirement; we'll add it to the partner ops checklist.

I'm attaching: Sample_Invoice_Template.pdf and a short guide for your AP on the CSV column order. Once you confirm acceptance of the fields, Marissa and I will queue legal for the addendum and loop in accounting to get a test settlement file.

Ben Carter
Director, Partnerships Operations | Redwood Inference
(attachment: Sample_Invoice_Template.pdf)
